release.about: main is both the integration branch and production for the static website: every merge redeploys GitHub Pages, so a merged change is live within minutes and the rollback is a revert. afo accepted that on 21 Nov 2026. His approval sits at production promotion instead, which no merge performs: the manual Fly deploys of the agent (packages/agent/fly.toml) and the Directus admin (packages/admin/fly.toml), migrations applied to the production database with db:migrate (recorded in audit.agent_schema_migrations), and Directus permission syncs against production (directus:content:setup, directus:content-access). Agents never run those; .agents/policy.json makes the shared guards ask first on afo's machine, and cloud agents hold no production credentials. The kit's merge-policy schema has no field for a gate by environment, so dev merge-settings does not apply this entry.

critical.about: Schema migrations, the steward permission model, the public projections, the Fly deploy configs and CI. Merges once three things hold on the current head: PR checks and every other required check are green, the full gate has passed (the Postgres migration job and rendered proof once they exist), and a fresh agent's adversarial review naming the head SHA is addressed. The agent merges by hand with that SHA as the expected head (gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <sha>) and stops if the head has moved; auto-merge would also merge a later push. Code-owner review cannot gate this tier, because GitHub refuses approval of one's own pull request.

sensitive.about: The rest of the agent runtime and shared contracts, the Directus admin package and the Directus scripts. Merges once the required checks are green and a fresh agent's adversarial review naming the head SHA is addressed, merged by hand with gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <sha>.

routine.about: Everything else: website, docs, plans, tests and tooling. Auto-merges once the required checks are green.
